sections.content: How many people are "speech and language therapists"?

14,240 people

were counted on the census as "speech and language therapists" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Speech and language therapists are responsible for the assessment, diagnosis and treatment of speech, language, fluency and voice disorders caused by disability, injury or illness.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "speech and language therapists" there were more women than men (96.6% compared with 3.4%).

This means "speech and language therapists" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 3.4% and women made up 96.6% of "speech and language therapists"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "speech and language therapists" included:

  • school secretaries
  • early education and childcare services managers
  • veterinary nurses

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "speech and language therapists", 19% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "speech and language therapists" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "speech and language therapists" included:

  • secondary education teaching professionals
  • primary education teaching professionals
  • natural and social science professionals (other)

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "speech and language therapists", 10.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (57.7% compared with 42.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (89.9%) than self-employed (10.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Sheffield, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
